title: Fine-Tuning & PEFT
html:
Updating weights to adapt models for specific formatting, behavior, and specialized tasks.

Fine-Tuning updates the model parameters. PEFT (Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning) updates a tiny subset of parameters (e.g., <1%) to make custom fine-tuning achievable on consumer hardware.

PEFT Methodologies

LoRA (Low-Rank Adaptation)

Instead of updating the full high-dimensional weight matrix (W0), LoRA freezes it and injects two smaller low-rank decomposition matrices (A and B) alongside it. This cuts trainable parameters by orders of magnitude (up to 10,000x for GPT-3 175B in the original paper) and greatly reduces GPU memory.

QLoRA (Quantized LoRA)

Enhances LoRA by quantizing the base model weights to 4-bit NormalFloat (NF4). It enables fine-tuning large models on a single GPU (e.g., 65B on one 48GB GPU) while largely matching 16-bit fine-tuning quality.

Adapters

Injecting small feed-forward layers after self-attention block layers. Only these newly added layer weights are trained; the rest of the base model layers are frozen.

When to RAG vs Fine-Tune

Factor RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) Fine-Tuning
Data Updates Dynamic (instantly reflects database updates) Static (requires retraining process to update data)
Source Citations Yes (can pinpoint retrieved source chunks) No (knowledge is baked into abstract weights)
Hallucination Risk Much lower (response is grounded in input context) Moderate (remains a statistical prediction)
Best for Accessing private facts, documentation search Adapting tone, formatting style, learning constraints
